explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM-generated feedback against human judgments by comparing correlation scores with human composite scores from the UniSumEval dataset, reporting both summary-level and system-level Spearman correlation metrics

prompts.notes: Full prompts provided in appendix tables for different configurations (C1-C4), including detailed instruction formats and JSON output requirements

guidelines.notes: Detailed annotation protocols provided including fact verification and key-fact alignment tasks, following established literature guidelines

sample_size.notes: Validation uses human composite scores from UniSumEval dataset as ground truth, but exact size of validation subset not explicitly stated

quantitative_scores.notes: Results shown in Table 3 with progressive improvement from C1 to C4 configurations, but exact correlation values not provided in main text

correlation_interpretation.interpretation: progressive improvement from low to high quality configurations

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-generated feedback quality shows progressive improvement with higher-quality configurations (C2-C4), with multi-dimensional fine-grained feedback (C4) demonstrating the best alignment with human judgments in composite scoring.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluations assess the same three core dimensions (faithfulness, completeness, conciseness) using percentage scores, though LLM evaluation also includes overall scoring
